name: Inclusion-exclusion for two and three sets
formula: |A \cup B| = |A| + |B| - |A \cap B| \qquad |A \cup B \cup C| = \textstyle\sum |A| - \sum |A \cap B| + |A \cap B \cap C|
whenToUse: Counting objects that satisfy at least one of several overlapping conditions, such as being divisible by $3$ or $5$.
example: Among $1$ to $100$ there are $33$ multiples of $3$, $20$ of $5$ and $6$ of $15$, so $33 + 20 - 6 = 47$ are multiples of $3$ or $5$.
pitfall: For divisibility, the overlap of multiples of $a$ and of $b$ is the multiples of $\operatorname{lcm}(a,b)$, which is not $ab$ unless $a$ and $b$ share no factor.
